photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print (black and white)
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Chief Washakie, a Shoshone leader, wearing traditional earrings, a large disc pendant, and garment — documentary photo of dress consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of two Shoshone men in traditional dress—tunics, hide leggings, moccasins, shell neck ornament, beaded hair wraps, and blankets—consistent with documentary photography of their daily dress and adornment.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Documentary portrait of a Shoshone chief (Washakie) in period dress seated before a tipi, a clear ethnographic photograph of daily/traditional life matching the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; carte-de-visite
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); carte-de-visite
photo.reason: Studio carte-de-visite portrait of Shoshone women and a child wearing cloth tunic dresses, seated on fur/hide garments — a documentary photo of dress and daily life consistent with the claimed people.

photo.name: postcard; photographic print
photo.title: postcard (black & white); photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary photo postcard of a Shoshone woman holding a baby in a traditional cradleboard/carrier, captioned "A Shoshone and Papoose," Reno NV 1940 — a genuine ethnographic snapshot of dress and material culture (the cradleboard) used by the people.

household.name: väska, bag
household.title: väska, bag
household.reason: A salmon-skin drawstring bag made by Cora George, a Tukudika (Sheepeater) Shoshone woman from Fort Hall, Idaho — a documented traditional Shoshone craft item made and attributed to a named tribal member.

instruments.name: Frame Drum
instruments.title: Frame Drum
instruments.reason: The image shows a wood-and-hide frame drum, a type of instrument consistent with Shoshone material culture; wood and rawhide construction fits plains/basin Native American traditions.

arms.name: bow, horn bow, arc
arms.title: bow, horn bow, arc
arms.reason: The image shows a horn bow, a weapon type the museum's own note identifies as characteristic of Shoshone, Crow, Blackfeet, Nez Perce, and Cheyenne peoples — consistent with the claimed Shoshone attribution.
